cohort: A cohort of 1,563 women in their third trimester of pregnancy were recruited from prenatal clinics.
finding: Restless legs syndrome significantly contributed to poor sleep quality, daytime sleepiness, and poor daytime function in pregnant women, with a dose-response relationship evident between RLS frequency and these disturbances, but no association was found with delivery outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no evidence for any association between RLS and delivery outcomes.
